_about: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for every closed vocabulary the vault enforces.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS (found 2026-10-17): vault-mcp.mjs hand-maintained a
VERBS array separate from its TOOLS catalogue. When `verify` was added to
TOOLS it was missed in VERBS, so tools/list ADVERTISED a tool that every
call rejected with 'has no adapter verb'. Visible and unreachable -- the
worst shape, because the failure surfaces at call time in a different code
path from the registration.
It was not a one-off. On the same date, six more closed vocabularies were
found duplicated across vault-lib.ps1 and vault-mcp.mjs, and ONE HAD ALREADY
DRIFTED: WriteFolders had four entries (incl. 'inbox') while the MCP create
enum had three. That one is deliberate -- see createFolders below -- but
nothing said so, so it was indistinguishable from a bug.
The rule: any two literals that must stay equal, maintained by hand, will
eventually disagree. Derive one from the other so drift is unrepresentable.
CONSUMERS
vault-lib.ps1   dot-sources this at load. FAILS CLOSED: a missing or
malformed registry throws before any verb runs.
vault-mcp.mjs   reads this at startup and derives every enum.
registry-test.ps1  guard tests. Its expectations are written as LITERALS,
never derived from this file -- a check built from the
thing it checks proves nothing. See that file's header.
_createFolders: NOT a subset bug. `create` may write only the three permanent folders;
`inbox` is reached via `propose`, which calls New-VaultNote -Folder 'inbox'
internally. The MCP create enum deliberately narrows to the three so an
agent cannot bypass the inbox's review queue by calling create directly.
PowerShell's guard keeps all four because propose depends on it.
Kept as two named lists rather than one so this difference stays EXPLAINED.
If you unify them, propose breaks or the inbox review queue becomes optional.
_immutableKeys: `verified` was REMOVED from the mutable set on 2026-10-17 on the joint
recommendation of two independent consultations. A model that can re-stamp
`verified` on a note it already wrote is certifying its own homework, and
git history keeps the unverified original while the note still READS as
verified. Re-verification is the `verify` verb's job.
`name` and `updated` are immutable for separate reasons: renaming means a
new note plus a supersede pointer, and `updated` is always today so an edit
`probe_*` is immutable because a probe the writer can tune after seeing its
result is a second opinion wearing a lab coat.
_probeSuites: `suite` names a test by ID and NEVER carries a command string. An arbitrary
command with the agent's authority behind it would make verify an injection
surface, which is strictly worse than having no verifier at all.
_verbs: The adapter's switch is the implementation; this list is the CONTRACT. The
contract lives here so the MCP layer can derive from it instead of keeping
its own copy. registry-test.ps1 calls every one of these against a scratch
vault and asserts none returns 'Unknown verb' -- an empirical check of the
